description: Past and planned lunar landing and impact sites, with the coordinates and caveats stated by each cited source
frame: planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude; sources state DE421 Mean Earth/Polar Axis (or LOLA 2011 for USGS feature centres)
coord_basis_note: 'reported landing/impact position' is a measured or published position of the object; 'region/feature centre' is the centre of a named feature near the intended destination and is not a landing target

sites.name: Apollo 11 — Tranquility Base
sites.coord_note: Lunar Module (descent stage) position measured in LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017); planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421. Five decimals (~3 m).

sites.name: Apollo 12 — Ocean of Storms
sites.coord_note: Lunar Module (descent stage) position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017); planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421; Surveyor 3 lies ~180 m away. Four decimals (~30 m digit resolution).

sites.name: Apollo 14 — Fra Mauro
sites.coord_note: Lunar Module (descent stage) position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017); planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421. Five decimals.

sites.name: Apollo 15 — Hadley-Apennine

sites.coord_note: Lunar Module (descent stage) position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017); planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421. Four decimals.

sites.name: Apollo 13 S-IVB impact
sites.coord_note: Centre of the Saturn V third-stage impact crater as measured by LROC; mean Earth/polar axis; LROC table gives 332.1125 E, converted to east-positive (-27.8875, same as NSSDC W column). Stated uncertainty 9.8 m.

sites.name: Apollo 14 S-IVB impact
sites.coord_note: LROC-measured S-IVB impact crater centre; mean Earth/polar axis; 333.9695 E converted to -26.0305. Stated uncertainty 4.5 m.

sites.name: Apollo 15 S-IVB impact
sites.coord_note: LROC-measured S-IVB impact crater centre; mean Earth/polar axis; 348.1755 E converted to -11.8245. Stated uncertainty 3.8 m.

sites.name: Apollo 16 S-IVB impact
sites.coord_note: LROC-measured S-IVB impact crater centre; mean Earth/polar axis; 335.3770 E converted to -24.6230. Stated uncertainty 19.2 m.

sites.name: Apollo 17 S-IVB impact
sites.coord_note: LROC-measured S-IVB impact crater centre; mean Earth/polar axis; 347.6693 E converted to -12.3307. Stated uncertainty 5.6 m.

sites.name: Surveyor 1 — Flamsteed P
sites.coord_note: Lander position measured in LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis; LROC gives 316.6602 E, converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 5.6 m; older NSSDC Surveyor page gives 2.45 S, 316.79 E.

sites.name: Surveyor 3 — Ocean of Storms
sites.coord_note: Lander position from LROC images (visited by Apollo 12); mean Earth/polar axis; 336.5820 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 2.6 m; older NSSDC Surveyor page gives 3.01 S, 336.66 E.

sites.name: Surveyor 5 — Mare Tranquillitatis
sites.coord_note: Lander position from LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 11.9 m; older NSSDC Surveyor page gives 1.41 N, 23.18 E.

sites.name: Surveyor 6 — Sinus Medii
sites.coord_note: Final lander position from LROC images (Surveyor 6 made a short 'hop' after landing); mean Earth/polar axis; 358.5725 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 6.7 m; older NSSDC page gives 0.49 N, 358.60 E.

sites.name: Surveyor 7 — Tycho north rim
sites.coord_note: Lander position from LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis; 348.4873 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 3.5 m; older NSSDC Surveyor page gives 40.86 S, 348.53 E (~4 km different).

sites.name: Ranger 6 impact — Mare Tranquillitatis
sites.coord_note: Impact crater centre measured by LROC; mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 4.4 m.

sites.name: Ranger 7 impact — Mare Cognitum
sites.coord_note: Impact crater centre measured by LROC; mean Earth/polar axis; 339.3230 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 6.4 m.

sites.name: Ranger 8 impact — Mare Tranquillitatis
sites.coord_note: Impact crater centre measured by LROC; mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 4.9 m.

sites.name: Ranger 9 impact — Alphonsus
sites.coord_note: Impact crater centre measured by LROC; mean Earth/polar axis; 357.6116 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 5.8 m.

sites.name: Lunar Prospector impact — south polar crater
sites.coord_note: Planned/estimated controlled-impact point (source: Ulivi and Harland 2004, per NSSDC footnote); not imaged; DE421 ME frame stated for the table. One decimal (~0.1 deg, km-scale).

sites.name: LCROSS / Centaur impact — Cabeus
sites.coord_note: Centaur upper-stage impact point in permanently shadowed Cabeus crater (not easily observable per NSSDC footnote); the LCROSS shepherding spacecraft hit nearby at 84.719 S, 49.61 W. DE421 ME frame stated for the table; four decimals.

sites.name: GRAIL-A (Ebb) impact
sites.coord_note: LROC-measured impact crater centre; mean Earth/polar axis; 333.4060 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 10.7 m.

sites.name: GRAIL-B (Flow) impact
sites.coord_note: LROC-measured impact crater centre; mean Earth/polar axis; 333.1659 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 12.2 m.

sites.name: LADEE impact — far side
sites.coord_note: LROC-measured impact crater centre; mean Earth/polar axis; 266.7506 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 6.1 m.

sites.name: Luna 2 impact — first object on the Moon
sites.coord_note: Approximate impact area only (Palus Putredinis, near Autolycus/Archimedes); NSSDC footnote says the site is uncertain, roughly 29-31 N, 1 W-1 E, Siddiqi (2018) says ~30 N / 0 on the slope of Autolycus, and the older NSSDC Soviet-missions page prints 29.10 N, 0.00. Not imaged; precision ~1 deg. Impact time 21:02:23 UT per Siddiqi (2018), who dates it 14 Sep 1959; the date here (13 Sep, UTC) follows the NSSDC 2025 table and NASA History (2019); the 2005 NSSDC page instead gives 14 Sep ~07:30 UT.

sites.name: Ranger 4 impact — far side
sites.coord_note: Predicted/tracked impact point of the uncontrolled spacecraft (first US craft to reach the Moon), not imaged; Siddiqi gives 15.5 S / 229.3 E at 12:49:53 UT, converted to east-positive (NSSDC prints 130.7 W). One decimal; real uncertainty likely larger.

sites.name: Luna 9 — Oceanus Procellarum
sites.coord_note: Historical value from an early Pravda report; NSSDC footnote says LROC images show no lander at these coordinates, so the true site is probably at least 10 km away. Printed to 0.01 deg but real uncertainty is >0.3 deg.

sites.name: Luna 13 — Oceanus Procellarum
sites.coord_note: Historical reported value (Siddiqi 2002/2018; Ulivi and Harland 2004, per NSSDC footnote), not LROC-confirmed; 297.95 E converted to east-positive. Two decimals; true accuracy likely coarser.

sites.name: Luna 16 — Mare Fecunditatis
sites.coord_note: Lander (descent stage) position measured in LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 3.7 m.

sites.name: Luna 17 — Mare Imbrium
sites.coord_note: Luna 17 lander (Lunokhod 1 carrier) position measured in LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis; 324.99837 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 0.5 m.

sites.name: Lunokhod 1 rover (final position)
sites.coord_note: Where the Lunokhod 1 rover stands as imaged by LROC (end of its traverse, not the landing point, which is the Luna 17 entry); mean Earth/polar axis; 324.9919 E converted. Stated uncertainty 3.8 m.

sites.name: Luna 18 crash — Mare Fecunditatis
sites.coord_note: NSSDC marks this as unconfirmed: contact was lost about 100 m above the surface and an object in an LROC image may be the lander. Two decimals.

sites.name: Luna 20 — Apollonius highlands
sites.coord_note: Lander position measured in LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 4.3 m.

sites.name: Luna 21 — Le Monnier
sites.coord_note: Luna 21 lander (Lunokhod 2 carrier) position from LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 13.4 m.

sites.name: Lunokhod 2 rover (final position)
sites.coord_note: Where the Lunokhod 2 rover stands as imaged by LROC (end of its traverse; landing point is the Luna 21 entry); mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 7.5 m.

sites.name: Luna 23 — Mare Crisium
sites.coord_note: Lander position from LROC images (landed damaged, no sample returned); mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 3.0 m.

sites.name: Luna 24 — Mare Crisium
sites.coord_note: Lander position from LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis. Stated uncertainty 3.7 m.

sites.name: Luna 25 crash — near Pontécoulant G
sites.coord_note: Crash crater imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Three decimals (~30 m).

sites.name: SMART-1 impact — Lacus Excellentiae
sites.coord_note: Impact point from Burchell et al. (2015) per NSSDC footnote; 313.8 E converted to east-positive. One decimal (~0.1 deg, ~3 km).

sites.name: Kaguya (SELENE) impact
sites.coord_note: Controlled-impact point from a 2009 JAXA press release per NSSDC footnote; not LROC-confirmed. One decimal.

sites.name: Chang'e 1 impact
sites.coord_note: Controlled-impact point from Xinhua (2009) per NSSDC footnote; Siddiqi (2018) gives 1.66 S, 52.27 E instead. Two decimals; not LROC-confirmed.

sites.name: Chang'e 3 — Mare Imbrium
sites.coord_note: Lander position measured in LROC images; mean Earth/polar axis; 340.4883 E converted to east-positive. Stated uncertainty 9.1 m.

sites.name: Yutu rover (final position)
sites.coord_note: Where the Yutu rover stands as imaged by LROC (a few tens of metres from the lander, after its short traverse); mean Earth/polar axis; 340.4878 E converted. Stated uncertainty 12.9 m.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 — Von Kármán crater (far side)
sites.coord_note: Lander position, imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Four decimals.

sites.name: Yutu-2 rover (deployment point)
sites.coord_note: Two-decimal position at the Chang'e 4 lander (rover deployment); NSSDC notes the rover was still mobile in Jan 2023 about 850 m NW of the lander, final coordinates TBD. DE421 ME frame.

sites.name: Chang'e 5 — Mons Rümker region
sites.coord_note: Lander (descent stage) position, imaged by LROC; DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Four decimals.

sites.name: Chang'e 6 — Apollo basin (far side)
sites.coord_note: Lander position computed by the LROC team from a 7 June 2024 image (stated horizontal accuracy +/-30 m); 206.0148 E converted to east-positive; frame not stated on LROC post, NSSDC gives same value in DE421 ME. NSSDC and LROC agree.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-2 Vikram crash site
sites.coord_note: Vikram impact point, imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Four decimals. Date is UTC (6 Sep), which is 7 Sep in India.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 — Shiv Shakti Point
sites.coord_note: Vikram lander position from LROC oblique image; frame not stated on LROC post (NSSDC lists same value in DE421 ME). Latitude to 4 decimals but longitude only 2 (~0.01 deg, ~100 m E-W at this latitude).

sites.name: SLIM — near Shioli crater
sites.coord_note: Lander position, imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Four decimals.

sites.name: ispace Hakuto-R Mission 1 crash — Atlas crater
sites.coord_note: Crash site imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Three decimals (~30 m).

sites.name: ispace Hakuto-R Mission 2 (Resilience) crash — Mare Frigoris
sites.coord_note: Crash site imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page; given as 4.588 W. Latitude 4 decimals, longitude 3.

sites.name: Beresheet crash — Mare Serenitatis
sites.coord_note: Impact site imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Four decimals.

sites.name: Intuitive Machines IM-1 Odysseus — Malapert A region
sites.coord_note: Lander position (landed tipped over), imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Only two decimals (~0.01 deg, ~300 m N-S).

sites.name: Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena — Mons Mouton region
sites.coord_note: Lander position (landed on its side), imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Four decimals.

sites.name: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 1 — Mare Crisium (Mons Latreille)
sites.coord_note: Lander position, imaged by LROC (NSSDC footnote d); DE421 mean Earth/polar axis per page. Three decimals (~30 m).

sites.name: Mons Mouton (Griffin-1 destination)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU feature Mons Mouton (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; feature diameter 130 km). NOT an agency landing target: NASA names only 'Mons Mouton (South Pole)' and publishes no coordinates. The date is the launch wording on NASA's Moon Base phases page (which credits Griffin-1 to 'Voyager Technologies'); the CLPS list still says 'in 2025'.

sites.name: Reiner Gamma
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU albedo feature Reiner Gamma (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; extent 73.44 km). NOT an agency landing target: NASA names only 'Reiner Gamma on the lunar nearside' and publishes no coordinates. As of 2026-11-14 the 'in 2026' wording on the CP-11 page has not been met.

sites.name: Schrödinger Basin
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU crater Schrödinger (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 316.39 km, so the true site could be over 150 km away). NOT an agency landing target: NASA names only 'Schrödinger Basin' and has not chosen a lander. The earlier CP-12 (Draper / ispace-U.S.) Schrödinger delivery is no longer listed on the CLPS page.

sites.name: Nassau crater (lunar far side)
sites.mission: Blue Ghost Mission 2 'Riders 2 the Dark' (CLPS CS-3/4)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU crater Nassau (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 75.80 km). NOT an agency landing target: Firefly says the landing site is 'near the Moon's Nassau crater'; NASA's CS-3 page says only 'lunar far side'. No coordinates published. The mission also carries the UAE's Rashid Rover 2 and ESA's Lunar Pathfinder. The date is Firefly's wording; NASA's CS-3 page still says 'in 2025'.

sites.name: Gruithuisen Domes (Gamma Dome)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU feature Mons Gruithuisen Gamma (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 19.65 km), chosen because Firefly says the mission will study 'the Gamma Dome'. NOT an agency landing target: NASA and Firefly name only 'the Gruithuisen Domes' and publish no coordinates. Date is Firefly's launch wording.

sites.name: Mons Mouton (IM-4 destination)
sites.agency: NASA (lander: Intuitive Machines Nova-C); ESA payload
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU feature Mons Mouton (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 130 km). NOT an agency landing target: NASA names only 'Mons Mouton' and publishes no coordinates. The payloads include ESA's PROSPECT. Date is the When field on NASA's IM-4 event page.

sites.name: Mons Mouton (VIPER destination)
sites.mission: VIPER on Blue Moon MK1 (CLPS CS-7)
sites.agency: NASA (lander: Blue Origin Blue Moon MK1)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU feature Mons Mouton (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 130 km). NOT an agency landing target: NASA says only that VIPER will be 'delivered to Mons Mouton' and publishes no coordinates. Date is the arrival wording on NASA's Moon Base phases page.

sites.name: Peak near Cabeus B (Artemis candidate region)
sites.mission: Artemis crewed landing (nine regions announced Oct 2024 for Artemis III; first landing now Artemis IV)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU crater Cabeus B (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 59.62 km). The NASA region is a peak NEAR this crater, not the crater centre. This is NOT an agency landing target, and NASA publishes no region coordinates. The regions were published for Artemis III, which NASA now lists as a 2027 test in low Earth orbit. The date is the Artemis IV launch wording, and that page cites 'nine candidate landing regions'.

sites.name: Haworth (Artemis candidate region)
sites.mission: Artemis crewed landing (nine regions announced Oct 2024 for Artemis III; first landing now Artemis IV)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU crater Haworth (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011 block, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 51.42 km). The same page's other control-network blocks give -86.90/-4.00 (UNKNOWN) and -87.20/-7.49 (ULCN 2005). This is NOT an agency landing target; NASA publishes no region coordinates. The regions were published for Artemis III (now a LEO test), and the date is the Artemis IV launch wording.

sites.name: Malapert Massif (Artemis candidate region)
sites.mission: Artemis crewed landing (nine regions announced Oct 2024 for Artemis III; first landing now Artemis IV)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU feature Mons Malapert (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 67 km; adopted 2024, 'Named for nearby crater, Malapert'). Matching NASA's 'Malapert Massif' to Mons Malapert is our identification; neither source states it. This is NOT an agency landing target; NASA publishes no region coordinates. The regions were published for Artemis III (now a LEO test), and the date is the Artemis IV launch wording.

sites.name: Mons Mouton (Artemis candidate region)
sites.mission: Artemis crewed landing (nine regions announced Oct 2024 for Artemis III; first landing now Artemis IV)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU feature Mons Mouton (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 130 km). NASA lists 'Mons Mouton' and 'Mons Mouton Plateau' as two separate regions. This feature centre stands in for neither specifically, and the Plateau is listed as unlocated. This is NOT an agency landing target; NASA publishes no region coordinates. The regions were published for Artemis III (now a LEO test), and the date is the Artemis IV launch wording.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1 / Nobile Rim 2 (Artemis candidate regions)
sites.mission: Artemis crewed landing (nine regions announced Oct 2024 for Artemis III; first landing now Artemis IV)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU crater Nobile (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 79.27 km). Both NASA regions lie on the RIM, roughly 40 km from this centre point, and the two are merged here because they share one feature source. This is NOT an agency landing target; NASA publishes no region coordinates. The regions were published for Artemis III (now a LEO test), and the date is the Artemis IV launch wording.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 2 (Artemis candidate region)
sites.mission: Artemis crewed landing (nine regions announced Oct 2024 for Artemis III; first landing now Artemis IV)
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU crater de Gerlache (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 32.71 km). The NASA region lies on the crater RIM, about 16 km from this centre. This is NOT an agency landing target; NASA publishes no region coordinates. The regions were published for Artemis III (now a LEO test), and the date is the Artemis IV launch wording.

sites.name: Shackleton crater (Chang'e-7 preferred candidate: Shackleton rim)
sites.program: Chinese Lunar Exploration Program (CLEP) / ILRS precursor
sites.coord_note: Centre of the IAU crater Shackleton (USGS Gazetteer, LOLA 2011, 'Planetographic, +East, -180 - 180'; diameter 20.92 km). The reported preferred candidate is the crater RIM, not its centre. This is NOT an agency landing target. CNSA has officially said only that the site is within 85°S (Zhao et al. 2025), and the Planetary Society says no final area has been announced. Date: Scientific American (24 Aug 2026) reports the launch is 'put on ice until at least 2027'. Wikipedia's 88.8°S 123.4°E (sourced to a 2023 Weibo post) is not used because it could not be traced to CNSA.

sites.name: MM-4, Mons Mouton area
sites.coord_note: Centre of the 1 km x 1 km MM-4 landing area, as printed by Space Applications Centre (ISRO) in LPSC 2026 abstract 1198 (Table-2 and text '(-84.289, 32.808)'). Sign convention as printed: negative latitude = south, positive longitude = east. The control network and reference frame are not stated. The abstract calls MM-4 a 'potential site'. PTI (9 Feb 2026) reports ISRO officials chose MM-4, and the chairman says 'targeting 2028'.

unlocated.name: Astrobotic Peregrine Mission One
unlocated.reason: Did not reach the lunar surface; no landing or impact site exists. Omitted per scope.

unlocated.name: Surveyor 2 (crash)
unlocated.reason: NSSDC impacts table gives only a coarse historical estimate (5.5 N, 12.0 W) not confirmed by LROC; NSSDC Surveyor page prints no coordinates. Left out as low-confidence.

unlocated.name: Surveyor 4 (crash)
unlocated.reason: NSSDC lists the site as 'Unknown' (parenthetical estimate 0.5 N, 1.5 W); contact lost 2.5 min before touchdown.

unlocated.name: Luna 15 (crash)
unlocated.reason: NSSDC gives 17 N, 60 E but footnote lists conflicting alternates (12 N 59 E; 17 N 49 E); not confirmed.

unlocated.name: Chang'e 5 ascent vehicle (deliberate impact)
unlocated.reason: NSSDC gives only '30. S, 0. E' with a note that it most likely hit at Regiomontanus crater; not a measured position.

unlocated.name: Chandrayaan-1 Moon Impact Probe
unlocated.reason: NSSDC footnote: impacted Shackleton crater area, exact coordinates unknown (table shows rounded 89 S, 30 W).

unlocated.name: Yutu-2 rover current/final position
unlocated.reason: NSSDC states final coordinates are TBD (rover ~850 m NW of Chang'e 4 as of Jan 2023); only the deployment point is listed.

unlocated.name: Apollo LM ascent stages and other Apollo hardware
unlocated.reason: Out of scope for this catalogue (NSSDC gives only seismic estimates or 'Unknown').

unlocated.name: Artemis candidate region: Mons Mouton Plateau
unlocated.reason: Named in NASA RELEASE 24-136 as separate from the 'Mons Mouton' region. It is not an IAU feature and NASA publishes no coordinates, so it is not given the Mons Mouton centre.

unlocated.name: Artemis candidate region: Slater Plain
unlocated.reason: Named in NASA RELEASE 24-136. 'Slater Plain' is not an IAU feature, and NASA publishes no coordinates. The IAU crater Slater (USGS Feature 15325) exists, but NASA does not say how the plain relates to it, so its centre is not used.

unlocated.name: Moon Base I: Blue Origin Blue Moon Mark 1 'Endurance'
unlocated.reason: NASA RELEASE 26-046 and the Moon Base phases page name 'Shackleton Connecting Ridge' as the landing site (no earlier than fall 2026). The ridge is not an IAU feature and neither NASA nor Blue Origin has published coordinates.

unlocated.name: CLPS CT-3: Blue Origin Blue Moon Mark 1
unlocated.reason: NASA CT-3 page (updated Nov 03, 2026) says only 'to the lunar south pole'. We could not confirm from a fetched page whether CT-3 is the Endurance / Shackleton Connecting Ridge flight.

unlocated.name: CLPS CS-6: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 4
unlocated.reason: NASA CS-6 page (updated Nov 05, 2026) says only 'the lunar south pole', with no site, coordinates or date.

unlocated.name: CLPS CT-4: Intuitive Machines Nova-D
unlocated.reason: The NASA CLPS deliveries list says only 'Lunar south pole' and there is no dedicated page. No site or coordinates.

unlocated.name: CLPS CS-8 (Moon Base payloads)
unlocated.reason: The NASA CLPS deliveries list names no provider and no location.

unlocated.name: CLPS CX-2 (Lunar Terrain Vehicle delivery)
unlocated.reason: The NASA CLPS deliveries list names no location. The Moon Base pages say LTVs are delivered in 2028 to the 'lunar South Pole region' with no named site.

unlocated.name: NASA MoonFall drones
unlocated.reason: The Moon Base phases page says the drones arrive at the South Pole in 2028 to survey potential Artemis sites. No site is named.

unlocated.name: Chang'e-8
unlocated.reason: Xinhua (english.spacechina.com, 2025-04-29) says it 'will target the Leibnitz-Beta Plateau near the lunar south pole region', launch 'around 2029'. Leibnitz-Beta is not a current IAU name. Its reported identity with Mons Mouton comes only from Wikipedia-derived pages and was not verified, so no coordinates are given.

unlocated.name: International Lunar Research Station (ILRS)
unlocated.reason: No named site with a fetched source was found; the Xinhua Chang'e-8 item only says it lays groundwork for ILRS.

unlocated.name: Luna 27 (Luna-Resurs-1 lander)
unlocated.reason: Only secondary or search-snippet text was found: an Acta Astronautica abstract describing a south-polar sector 51°E-1°W, 83°S-79°S with 'Site №1'. The abstract page could not be read (X-MOL placeholder), and no Roscosmos/IKI page with a site was fetched.

unlocated.name: Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX (ISRO-JAXA)
unlocated.reason: South polar mission. The only coordinate seen (89.45°S, 222.85°E, from a 2024 talk) appeared in a search snippet from a secondary blog and was not fetched from ISRO or JAXA, so it is not used.

unlocated.name: ispace Mission 5 (formerly ispace-U.S. Mission 3 / APEX 1.0, Team Draper, CLPS CP-12)
unlocated.reason: ispace's 27 Mar 2026 release moves it to 2030, pending NASA approval, and names no site. The earlier Schrödinger Basin target was seen only in a search snippet of ispace-us.com (the fetched homepage names no site), and CP-12 no longer appears on NASA's CLPS list.

unlocated.name: ispace Mission 3 (2028) and Mission 4 (2029)
unlocated.reason: ispace's 27 Mar 2026 release gives launch years only. Mission 4 relates to 'High-Precision Landing Technology in the Lunar Poles', but no site is named.

unlocated.name: ESA Argonaut, KARI (South Korea) lunar lander, other national landers
unlocated.reason: Not researched in depth this session, and no fetched page naming a landing site was found.
